items.title: [Cariboo Signals Reviews] Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, October 7, 2026
items.content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 37591489581.

Cohere embeddings offline; fallback paths held

The primary run at 1:05 AM completed successfully, but three separate steps in the script generation stage lost access to Cohere's embedding service. The pipeline detected a ModuleNotFoundError and fell back to keyword-based ranking in all three cases: evolving-story detection, same-story clustering, and deep-dive reranking.

The cost was visible only in the last step. The deep-dive rerank kept its keyword ranking instead of the reranked order. Of the three deep dives that aired — an iFixit teardown, a creatine study, and a Gaza journalism piece — only 1 of 3 citations aligned with sources. The roundup maintained perfect citation matching at 15 of 15, suggesting the keyword fallback worked adequately for shorter stories but degraded on longer investigative pieces.

Script undershoot and expand

The first draft arrived at 1,939 words against a target of 3,400. The pipeline sent it back for one expand pass. The shipped version landed at 2,913 words — still 487 words short of target, but 974 words longer than the draft.

This gap between target and shipped is the largest tension in the run. The audio rendered to 16.9 minutes regardless. No mechanism in the facts states why the second pass stopped short of the full target.

TTS retry loop: two segments still short

Three text-to-speech takes came back shorter than their word counts predicted. The pipeline retried each once. Two of those retries still ran short. The longer take from each pair was kept, so neither segment was dropped from the episode.

R2 sync broke one asset link

During publishing, one object referenced by podcast-feed.xml could not be found in R2 storage and could not be healed from disk. Crawlers requesting that object will receive a 404. The RSS feed points to 252 total episodes; this broken reference is live in the feed.

Voice balance and quality patterns

Casey's airtime exceeded Riley's by a ratio of 1.01 to 1. One AI tell pattern hit during quality review. The script shipped at 2,913 words across 16.9 minutes of audio and 15.5 MB of file size. Video rendered to 16.9 minutes at 58.1 MB.

Roundup pool depth and story cutoff

Fifty-two stories were dropped from the roundup pool by the airtime budget. This is by design — the candidate pool runs larger than a single segment can air, and cut stories can surface on better-matched days. The debate question for the day: how should rural communities measure equipment repairability and reliability beyond standardized spec sheets and online review scores?

items.title: [Cariboo Signals Reviews] Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, October 5, 2026
items.content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 37287761323.

Primary run failed; fallback succeeded with Cohere embed failures

The 1:05 AM primary run did not complete. The 2:05 AM fallback (run 37287761323) finished in 23 minutes with a success conclusion. That run is the source of all shipped content below.

Three Cohere embedding operations failed with ModuleNotFoundError during script generation. The pipeline fell back to non-Cohere paths for evolving-story detection and same-story clustering. For deep-dive reranking, it kept the keyword ranking instead. These degradations mean the script used simpler clustering and ranking than designed, but produced output.

Script expanded after first draft came short

The first draft measured 2785 words against a 3400-word target. The script was sent back for expansion and shipped at 3184 words. The target was not met, but the gap closed from 615 words to 216 words.

One TTS segment returned shorter than its word count predicted. It was retried once per protocol and included in the final audio.

Citation coverage complete; story ordering still imperfect

All 15 roundup citations matched their sources. All 3 deep-dive citations matched. The pipeline found no reference gaps in either segment.

Five stories still aired out of intended order after one repair pass in the roundup-order step. This is a recurring degradation: the reordering logic has not fully stabilized.

Deep dives and debate

Three deep dives shipped: MoMA on information design (Fast Company), a Man in Motion film screening (Williams Lake Tribune), and a Putin disinformation operation narrative (Mother Jones).

The debate question: Should arts and cultural organizations rely primarily on quantitative metrics like attendance counts to measure value and success, or should they prioritize qualitative community input and contextual understanding?

Audio, video, and distribution

The episode ran 18.4 minutes of audio and video. Audio file: 16.9 MB. Video file: 63.3 MB. This episode marked RSS entry 250.

One object referenced by podcast-feed.xml is missing from Cloudflare R2 and cannot be healed from disk. Crawlers will 404 on that asset.

Quality and voice balance

Casey spoke 1.01 times as much as Riley — near parity. The script triggered one AI-tell pattern hit during quality review.

Compute and API calls

The run consumed 50,860 Anthropic input tokens across 13 Claude calls. Search and answers came from 7 Brave Search calls and 5 Brave Answers calls.

Roundup pool held 49 more stories than the airtime budget allowed. Those 49 stories were cut and remain available for later matching.
